title: Embedded integral constant scalar square and residue kernel
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E$ be a finite intermediate field of $\operatorname{PadicAlgCl}(\ell)$, equip $\operatorname{ULift} E$ with its finite-dimensional $\mathbf Q_\ell$-algebra structure, and let $\pi\in\mathcal O_E$ generate its maximal ideal. Use the embedded constant and continuous coefficient maps [def-sfb-embedded-integral-model-coefficients] and the spectral coefficient maps [def-sfb-integral-models-stacks-data]. Let $e$ be any isomorphism from the condensed commutative ring of continuous embedded integers to the condensed spectral integer ring of $\operatorname{ULift} E$, and let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme in universe $u$. There is an isomorphism $a$ from the pulled-back constant spectral integer ring to the pulled-back constant embedded integer ring such that $a$ followed by the embedded constant-to-continuous map equals the spectral constant-to-continuous map followed by the inverse image of $e^{-1}$. Extension along the small section-ring map of $a$ carries the spectral first residue kernel ideal [def-sfb-quotient-kernel-completeness] to the embedded first residue kernel ideal. This is an underived ring and ideal statement, independent of complexes or completeness.

source.place: Displayed criterion: transport of the local completeness and first-residue predicates; Stacks Tag 09C1.

proof.text: Regard the given internal monoid isomorphism as an isomorphism of ring-valued sheaves: its additive section isomorphisms preserve multiplication by the monoidal sheaf-to-presheaf functor. Evaluate its inverse on the one-point profinite set and use the constant-function identifications to obtain a ring isomorphism from spectral integers to embedded integers. Express each constant-to-continuous map as the counit of the constant-sheaf/point-sections adjunction. Naturality of this counit and of constant sheafification with respect to forgetting commutativity gives the scalar square. Apply the coefficient inverse-image functor to obtain a.

The DVR description identifies the spectral first quotient ideal with its maximal ideal. A ring isomorphism sends that maximal ideal to the embedded maximal ideal, identified with the span of the chosen uniformizer by the hypothesis. The induced quotient ring isomorphism gives a commuting square with the first quotient maps; apply constant sheafification, coefficient inverse image and the small section-ring functor to this square. Prove generally that a commuting square whose horizontal arrows are ring-sheaf isomorphisms transports the kernel ideal by extension: sectionwise the image kernel generates precisely the other kernel, and the local characterization uniquely specifies ideal extension. Apply this fact to the small section-ring square.

lean.statement:
theorem embeddedIntegralScalarKernelSquare
    (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] (E : PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField ℓ)
    [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[ℓ] (ULift.{u} E.val)]
    (π : PadicAlgCl.integers ℓ E.1)
    (hπ : Ideal.span {π} = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (PadicAlgCl.integers ℓ E.1))
    (e : Mon.mk (Profinite.padicIntegersRingObj.{u} ℓ E.val) ≅
      sfbCondensedIntegers ℓ (ULift.{u} E.val))
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] :
    ∃ a : Mon.mk (condensedRingObj
        (IntegralModelsStacks.discreteObj
          (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers ℓ (ULift.{u} E.val))) X) ≅
      Mon.mk (condensedRingObj
        (IntegralModelsEmbedded.discreteObj (PadicAlgCl.integers ℓ E.1)) X),
      a.hom.hom ≫ IntegralModelsEmbedded.scalarMap ℓ E X =
        IntegralModelsStacks.scalarMap ℓ (ULift.{u} E.val) X ≫
          (upperStarFromPoint X).map e.inv.hom ∧
      (ConstantCompletion.kernelIdeal (IntegralModelsStacks.smallMap X
        (IntegralModelsStacks.residueMap ℓ (ULift.{u} E.val) X))).extension
          (IntegralModelsStacks.smallMap X a.hom.hom) =
        ConstantCompletion.kernelIdeal (IntegralModelsStacks.smallMap X
          (IntegralModelsEmbedded.residueMap ℓ E π X))
